title: Consensus
explain: Consensus is how a group of nodes agrees on a single ordered sequence of decisions, usually log entries, even though nodes crash and messages are delayed. Everyone applies the same entries in the same order, so every replica of a state machine reaches the same state.
model:
The shape is always the same:

```
1 leader proposes an entry
2 replicates it to a quorum
3 once a majority has it: COMMITTED ─▶ every replica applies in order
```

Quorum overlap stops two different decisions from both succeeding. Families: **Paxos**, [Raft](#/sd/f/raft) and **ZAB** (ZooKeeper). See [quorum](#/sd/f/quorum).

**Guarantees:**

- **Agreement and validity (safety):** no two nodes decide differently, and a decided value was actually proposed. Safety holds even when timing assumptions break.
- **Progress (liveness):** decisions happen while a majority is alive and can talk and timing is reasonable. A partitioned minority stalls.

**Costs:** at least one majority round trip per decision, 2f + 1 nodes for f failures, and no answers without a majority.

**Use it for small, critical coordination data:** who the leader is ([leader election](#/sd/f/leader-election)), configuration, shard maps, locks and [leases](#/sd/f/lease). **Don't** run bulk data or every user click through it; replicate that normally and keep consensus for the metadata that decides who owns what.

details.q: What is the difference between consensus and plain replication?
details.a: Plain replication copies data; consensus makes the replicas agree on one order of decisions even under crashes and partitions. Leader election, locks and config changes need agreement, not just copies.

details.q: A 5-node cluster is split into 3 and 2. What should a client writing to the 2-node side see?
details.a: An error or timeout. The minority side cannot form a majority, so it must not commit; it may redirect or wait for the partition to heal.

details.q: Why not make the leader wait for all replicas to ack?
details.a: One slow or dead replica would stall every commit. A majority is enough for safety (overlap) and keeps the slowest replicas off the critical path.

details.q: How long does a commit take with leader RTTs of 2, 6, 40 and 90 ms to four followers?
details.a: About 6 ms. In 5 nodes a majority is 3: the leader plus the two fastest followers. The 40 and 90 ms followers do not matter (ignoring disk and processing).

details.q: What are safety and liveness here?
details.a: Safety: agreement and validity, never violated even under bad timing. Liveness: progress, which needs a majority alive and reasonable timing. Consensus sacrifices liveness, not safety, in a partition.

details.q: What should and should not go through consensus?
details.a: Should: leader election, configuration, shard maps, locks, leases. Should not: bulk data and user traffic; replicate those normally and use consensus only for the metadata deciding ownership.

prompts.q: Explain what consensus guarantees, what it costs, and what not to use it for.
points: Single ordered sequence, agreement and validity
Progress needs a majority and decent timing
Majority round trip per decision, 2f + 1 nodes
Use for leader, config, locks, shard maps

prompts.q: Walk through one decision in a leader-based consensus protocol.
Explain what happens during a partition in a 5-node consensus group.
points: 3-node side keeps a majority and continues
Safety preserved, liveness sacrificed on the minority
Heal: minority catches up from the log
